title: Methods for Protecting Earth against an Asteroid Strike
titleZh: 保护地球免受小行星撞击的方法
credits: Daniel Lawler with Issam Ahmed reported this story for Agence France-Presse. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sentences.en: Astronomers following asteroid activity in space estimate there is a very small chance an object large enough to destroy a whole city could strike Earth in 2032.
sentences.zh: 天文学家正在追踪太空中的小行星活动，据估计，一颗足以摧毁整座城市的巨大物体在2032年撞击地球的概率非常小。

sentences.en: But space agency officials say even if such an asteroid keeps heading on a path toward Earth, the world is now much better-equipped to defend itself against such a threat.
sentences.zh: 但航天机构官员表示，即便这样一颗小行星持续朝着地球的方向飞行，如今世界已具备更强的能力来抵御此类威胁。

sentences.en: The American space agency NASA recently estimated there was a 3.1 percent chance that asteroid 2024 YR4 would hit Earth on December 22, 2032.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局NASA最近估计，小行星2024 YR4在2032年12月22日撞击地球的概率为3.1%。

sentences.en: That is the highest probability predicted for such a large space rock in modern times.
sentences.zh: 这是现代史上对如此巨大的太空岩石预测出的最高概率。

sentences.en: Richard Moissl is head of the European Space Agency's (ESA) planetary defense office.
sentences.zh: 理查德·莫斯尔是欧洲航天局（ESA）行星防御办公室主任。

sentences.en: While recognizing the risk the asteroid could present, he told the French news agency AFP people should not panic over such predictions.
sentences.zh: 他在承认这颗小行星可能带来风险的同时，向法国新闻社法新社表示，人们不必因这类预测而恐慌。

sentences.en: Astronomers have noted that the more data they gather, the odds of a direct asteroid hit are expected to keep rising over time.
sentences.zh: 天文学家指出，他们收集的数据越多，小行星直接撞击地球的概率预计会随时间推移而持续上升。

sentences.en: However, scientists say at a certain point the odds will likely drop down to zero.
sentences.zh: 然而，科学家表示，在某个特定时刻，这一概率很可能会降至零。

sentences.en: Moissl said he thinks it is important to remember that even in the unlikely event the probability keeps rising to 100 percent, the world is "not defenseless."
sentences.zh: 莫斯尔表示，他认为重要的是要记住，即便在概率持续上升至100%这种极不可能的情况下，世界也"并非毫无防御能力"。

sentences.en: Here are some methods currently being considered as defensive measures to keep humanity safe in case there is a real threat.
sentences.zh: 以下是目前正在考虑作为防御措施的一些方法，以防存在真实威胁时保护人类安全。

sentences.en: Only one planetary defense method has been tried against an asteroid.
sentences.zh: 目前只有一种行星防御方法曾用于小行星。

sentences.en: In 2022, NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) sent a spacecraft into the 160-meter-wide Dimorphos asteroid.
sentences.zh: 2022年，NASA的双小行星重定向测试（DART）任务将一艘航天器送入宽约160米的迪莫尔福斯小行星。

sentences.en: The effort successfully changed the asteroid’s orbit around a larger space rock.
sentences.zh: 这一努力成功改变了该小行星围绕更大太空岩石的轨道。

sentences.en: Bruce Betts is chief scientist for the nonprofit Planetary Society.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·贝茨是非营利组织行星学会的首席科学家。

sentences.en: He told AFP that space agencies could hit the 2024 YR4 asteroid with several spacecrafts, observing how each one changed the path.
sentences.zh: 他告诉法新社，航天机构可以用多艘航天器撞击2024 YR4小行星，并观察每艘航天器如何改变其运行轨道。

sentences.en: The asteroid discovered in December is estimated to be 40-90 meters wide -- about half the size of Dimorphos.
sentences.zh: 这颗于12月发现的小行星估计宽约40至90米——约为迪莫尔福斯的一半。

sentences.en: "You have to take care not to overdo it," Moissl warned.
sentences.zh: 莫斯尔警告说："你必须注意不要做得过头。"

sentences.en: He said this is because if a spacecraft only partly destroys an asteroid, it could send smaller pieces of the space rock heading toward Earth.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是因为如果航天器只部分摧毁了小行星，就可能使太空岩石的较小碎片朝地球飞来。

sentences.en: A separate idea would involve sending a large spacecraft to fly alongside a threatening asteroid.
sentences.zh: 另一个独立的设想是发射一艘大型航天器，在威胁性小行星旁伴飞。

sentences.en: The spacecraft would not touch the asteroid, but would use its gravitational force to pull it away from Earth.
sentences.zh: 航天器不会接触小行星，而是利用自身的引力将其拉离地球。

sentences.en: Moissl said another non-contact plan would put a spacecraft near the asteroid to eject a continuous flow of atoms to push the asteroid off course.
sentences.zh: 莫斯尔说，另一种非接触方案是让一艘航天器靠近小行星，持续喷射原子流，从而把小行星推离轨道。

sentences.en: Scientists have also considered painting one side of the asteroid white.
sentences.zh: 科学家们还考虑过把小行星的一面涂成白色。

sentences.en: They believe this could increase the light the object reflects to make it slowly change course.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这可能会增加该物体反射的光，使其缓慢改变轨道。

sentences.en: One idea is to use a nuclear weapon against a threatening asteroid.
sentences.zh: 一个想法是用核武器对付具有威胁性的小行星。

sentences.en: In laboratory tests, researchers found that X-rays from a nuclear blast could move a rock.
sentences.zh: 在实验室测试中，研究人员发现核爆炸产生的X射线可以推动一块岩石。

sentences.en: But this is considered more of a plan for kilometers-wide asteroids like the one that killed off the dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 但这被认为更像是针对数公里宽的小行星的方案，就像当年导致恐龙灭绝的那颗。

sentences.en: And this method also carries the risk that a nuclear explosion could send additional pieces of the asteroid falling toward Earth.
sentences.zh: 而且这种方法还承担着核爆炸可能把小行星的更多碎片抛向地球的风险。

sentences.en: A similar method – but one considered less dangerous – would involve shooting laser beams from a spacecraft to destroy the side of an asteroid in an effort to push it away from Earth.
sentences.zh: 一种类似的方法——但被认为危险性较低——将涉及从航天器发射激光束，摧毁小行星的一侧，从而把它推离地球。

sentences.en: Moissl said that if all else fails, at least the world will have a good idea where a threatening asteroid would strike.
sentences.zh: 莫斯尔说，如果其他方法都失败，至少世界会清楚地知道一颗威胁性小行星会在哪里撞击。

sentences.en: Since astronomers believe most asteroids would at most threaten to destroy one city, efforts could be organized to get people out of an area before a strike.
sentences.zh: 由于天文学家认为大多数小行星至多会威胁摧毁一座城市，因此可以组织努力，在撞击之前把人们疏散出相关区域。

sentences.en: "Seven-and-a-half years is a long time to prepare," Moissl added.
sentences.zh: 莫斯尔补充说：'七年半是很长的准备时间。'

sentences.en: He also noted that even with the rising odds involving 2024 YR4, there is still about a 97 percent chance the asteroid will miss Earth.
sentences.zh: 他还指出，尽管涉及2024 YR4的概率在上升，但小行星错过地球的概率仍有约97%。

sentences.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

glossary.def: any of the small rocky celestial bodies found especially between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
of light or sound. to move in one direction, hit a surface, and then quickly move in a different and usually opposite direction
